papers.title: A nonsense variant in KCNH7 (c.1324 C>T) is associated with a variable phenotypic spectrum of epilepsy.
papers.abstract: KCNH7 is a voltage-gated potassium (K+) channel (Kv) that regulates membrane excitability and K+ flux across tissues. Studies using mouse models have suggested that Kcnh7 may play an important role in epilepsy susceptibility and pathogenesis. However, clinical and experimental evidence implicating KCNH7 variants in human epilepsy, as well as the genotype-phenotype association, remains unclear. Here, we aimed to refine the clinical, genetic, and functional electrophysiological features of a p.R442* variant identified in three individuals to elucidate potential genotype-phenotype association that may guide anticipatory management. We generated Kcnh7 mutants​ using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing. Heterozygous mutants exhibited increased neuronal hyperexcitability and increased seizure susceptibility due to reduced Kcnh7-encoded protein levels. Functional analyses established the KCNH7 p.R442* variant as a loss-of-function allele, with haploinsufficiency identified as a primary pathogenic mechanism. Our results underscore the significance of functional characterization for the KCNH7 p.R442* variant within the context of clinical interpretation, although larger cohorts are required to further validate these observations.

papers.title: Association between neonatal phototherapy and childhood epilepsy and febrile seizures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Phototherapy has been widely used for the treatment of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia. However, concerns persist about its long-term neurological effects. While some studies report an increased risk of epilepsy after phototherapy, others found no association. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to examine the association between phototherapy and childhood epilepsy and febrile seizures. We followed the PRISMA guidelines for our meta-analysis. We searched six databases for studies investigating the association between phototherapy and childhood epilepsy and febrile seizures. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used for quality assessment. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effect model in R software. Three studies with 632,227 participants met our inclusion criteria. Phototherapy was associated with a 37% higher risk of childhood epilepsy (HR = 1.37, 95% CI = 1.13-1.67, p < 0.01; I2 = 30%). Subgroup analysis revealed a significant risk in boys (HR = 1.62, 95% CI = 1.17-2.24, p < 0.01) but not girls (HR = 1.14, 95% CI = 0.92-1.41, p = 0.23). No association was found with febrile seizures (HR = 1.07, 95% CI = 0.99-1.15, p = 0.09).
CONCLUSION: In this meta-analysis of three observational cohorts, neonatal phototherapy was associated with a possible increase in the risk of childhood epilepsy, particularly in boys; this finding depends on a small and methodologically heterogeneous evidence base, and residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded. Given the limited number of studies, the conflicting result from the most methodologically rigorous study, and the exploratory nature of the sex-stratified analysis, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as grounds to alter current phototherapy practice. Further well-designed studies controlling for confounders are needed.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Phototherapy is standard treatment for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and is generally considered safe. • Prior studies on phototherapy and childhood epilepsy have shown conflicting results.
WHAT IS NEW: • Pooled analysis of 632,227 infants show an association between phototherapy and childhood epilepsy, particularlyin boys, but not febrile seizures. • The association may reflect residual confounding rather than a causal effect, and does not currently justify changingphototherapy practice.

papers.title: Long-Term Neurologic Complication and Healthcare Burden in Infants Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study.
papers.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate survival, neurologic complications, and healthcare burden in infant extracorporeal life support (ECLS) recipients using nationally representative administrative data from a single-payer healthcare system.
DESIGN: Retrospective, population-based cohort study.
SETTING: South Korea's National Health Insurance Service, covering 97% of the population.
PATIENTS: Infants under 1 year who received ECLS between 2009 and 2022.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 698 infants who underwent ECLS, 212 infants (30.4%) survived during follow-up (estimated 1-yr mortality: 67.1%). Among survivors, 128 (60.4%) developed neurologic injuries, including acute events such as ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI), as well as long-term sequelae such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, hearing loss, and developmental delay. Most acute neurologic injuries were diagnosed within the first year, whereas developmental delay showed prolonged diagnostic windows extending up to 12 years. Survivors with neurologic injury had significantly longer hospital stays (432.1 vs. 182.3 d; p < 0.001) and higher cumulative healthcare costs during long-term follow-up. Median index hospitalization costs were USD 36,000-37,000. The burden analysis showed distinct profiles across neurologic complications: developmental delay was the most prevalent sequela, whereas HIBI was associated with the highest cumulative healthcare cost despite lower prevalence.
CONCLUSIONS: Neurologic complications following ECLS in infants are common and impose substantial long-term healthcare burden. These findings highlight the need for early risk stratification, structured neurologic and neurodevelopmental monitoring, and sustained rehabilitation planning in this high-risk population. This study provides a foundation for international benchmarking and health policy planning in pediatric critical care.

papers.title: [Medication dose adjustment in obesity: lessons from practice].
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of obesity complicates appropriate drug dosing. We describe patient with obesity who developed aciclovir-induced renal and neurotoxicity, culminating in status epilepticus for which he required ICU admission. In this case, dosing was based on total body weight, which likely resulted in overdosing of this hydrophilic, renally cleared drug. In contrast, we present a patient with obesity who was successfully treated with voriconazole for invasive aspergillosis following septic shock. Given the drug's interindividual variability, dosing was based on the adjusted body weight and therapeutic drug monitoring was performed. Obesity induces clinically relevant physiological changes affecting drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination. However, these effects are heterogeneous and drug-specific, limiting the utility of simple weight-based dosing strategies. We conclude that drug dosing in patients with obesity requires an individualized approach based on pharmacokinetic principles. Early involvement of a clinical pharmacist and, where available, therapeutic drug monitoring are strongly recommended.

papers.title: Synaptic Transmission Onto Somatostatin Interneurons Is Enhanced Under Acidic Conditions in an Elfn1-Dependent Manner.
papers.abstract: Somatostatin (SOM) interneurons regulate hyperexcitability by producing inhibitory feedback when brain activity becomes excessive. SOM inhibitory feedback depends on the cooperative activity of two synaptic proteins: Elfn1 (extracellular leucine rich repeat and fibronectin type III domain containing 1) and mGluR7 (metabotropic glutamate receptor 7). Elfn1 knockout (KO) mice experience seizures, and humans with ELFN1 mutations are at risk of epilepsy. Seizures can increase brain acidity, and mGluR7 can be inhibited by acidity. Elfn1 and mGluR7 normally act together to transiently suppress SOM interneuron recruitment and previous work showed that inhibiting mGluR7 increases excitatory transmission onto SOM interneurons. We hypothesized that acidity would disrupt mGluR7 activity to increase excitatory transmission onto SOM interneurons. Whole-cell recordings in cortical slices showed that acidity increased putative excitatory input onto SOM interneurons and decreased paired-pulse ratio (PPR), an effect that is absent in Elfn1 KO mice. Conversely, putative excitatory transmission onto excitatory cells in wild-type mice was decreased under acidic conditions, without changes in PPR. Overall, we show how Elfn1/mGluR7 change SOM interneuron responses to acidic environments to enhance inhibition while reducing excitation.

papers.title: Autistic Adolescents and Associate Medical Conditions.
papers.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder is a neurological and developmental condition impacting 1 in 31 children. Children, identified on the autism spectrum, are typically diagnosed by the age of 8; however, research indicates that there could be as many as 25% of undiagnosed adolescents. Autistic adolescents have a significantly higher prevalence of mental-health and medical conditions than their neurotypical peers including gastrointestinal disorders (e.g., chronic constipation), seizure disorders, sleep disturbances, and nutritional disorders (e.g., overeating). Part-1, "Interventions for Adolescent Students with Autism and Co-Occurring Mental Health Disorders," of this three-part series discussed interventions for the mental health comorbidities often experienced by autistic adolescents. This second article will address common medical conditions experienced by autistic adolescents and how school nurses can help manage these conditions in school settings.

papers.title: Caregiver Burden in Highly Complex Pediatric Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: Associations With Functional Status and Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy.
papers.abstract: Background Caregiver burden is an important consequence of caring for children with highly complex drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). Although greater functional impairment may increase caregiving demands, burden may also be influenced by developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) and caregiver characteristics. We aimed to estimate caregiver burden and determine whether child functional status remained associated with burden after accounting for DEE and caregiver characteristics. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analytical study of 59 child-caregiver dyads with highly complex DRE attending a national high-specialty medical center in Mexico City between November 2025 and February 2026. Caregiver burden was assessed using the 22-item Zarit Burden Interview (ZBI), with scores >46 defining overburden. Child functional status was assessed using the Functional Status Scale (FSS). DEE was classified according to an operational definition incorporating frequent seizures and/or epileptiform discharges, developmental slowing or regression, and an underlying etiology contributing to developmental impairment. Logistic regression models evaluated threshold-defined overburden, and a complementary linear model examined continuous ZBI scores. Results Overburden was present in 40/59 caregivers (67.8%; 95% CI, 54.4%-79.4%). Among 54 children with available FSS assessments, FSS scores were higher in dyads with overburden than in those without (median 11 (IQR, 9-20) vs 8 (IQR, 7-11.5); p = 0.021). However, the correlation between FSS and continuous ZBI scores was weak and not significant (rho = 0.165; p = 0.233). FSS was associated with overburden in the univariable model (OR per point, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.01-1.29), but this association attenuated after inclusion of DEE and caregiver characteristics and was not significant in the combined model (OR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.93-1.22). In the combined model, DEE (OR, 8.38; 95% CI, 1.14-61.85) and caregiver age per 10 years (OR, 4.51; 95% CI, 1.26-16.12) were associated with overburden. In the continuous ZBI model, caregiver age was associated with higher burden (B = 6.49 points per 10 years; 95% CI, 1.59-11.39), as was parental caregiver status (B = 13.68; 95% CI, 2.19-25.16), whereas FSS and DEE were not independently associated with continuous ZBI scores. Individual FSS domains showed no consistent association with burden. Conclusions Caregiver overburden was frequent in this Mexican cohort of children with highly complex DRE. Although poorer functional status distinguished caregivers with overburden before adjustment, its association weakened after consideration of DEE and caregiver characteristics and was not observed when burden was analyzed continuously. DEE showed a large but imprecise association with threshold-defined overburden, whereas caregiver age was consistently associated with both categorical and continuous measures of burden. These findings suggest that caregiver burden should be understood as a distinct caregiver-level outcome within the broader clinical and family context of highly complex pediatric DRE, rather than solely as a consequence of the child's functional impairment.

papers.title: Predictors of Anesthetic Augmentation in Electroconvulsive Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Anesthetic augmentation with aminophylline and/or remifentanil is commonly used to prolong seizure duration when propofol-based electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) results in inadequate seizures. We aimed to identify independent predictors of subsequent augmentation use and develop an exploratory risk score. Methods: This retrospective cohort study (January-December 2015, single center) included 527 patients (4,016 ECT sessions) who received propofol anesthesia. Patients were categorized as propofol-only (n=357) or augmentation (n=170) group. Multiple logistic regression was used to identify predictors of augmentation. ANCOVA compared the effect of different adjunctive agents on post-adjunct seizure duration. Results: Shorter first-session electroencephalography (EEG) seizure duration (OR = 0.968, P < .001) and higher first-session seizure-inducing energy (OR = 1.044, P < .001) independently predicted augmentation, while age was not significant (P = .120). All three augmentation strategies significantly prolonged seizure duration; although, the sample sizes for individual agents (aminophylline n=85, remifentanil n=44, combination n=41) precluded a definitive comparative analysis; the ANCOVA revealed no significant differences between agents (F=0.967, P = .382). CGI scores were comparable between groups at baseline (P = .412) and discharge (P = .321). An exploratory risk score based on the two significant predictors showed good discriminative ability (AUC = 0.786). Conclusion: First-session EEG seizure duration and stimulation energy are practical predictors of subsequent augmentation use, whereas age is not independently predictive. No statistically significant difference in post-adjunct seizure duration was detected among the three adjunctive strategies and augmentation is associated with comparable clinical improvement. External validation of the proposed risk score is required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Detection of Acute Myocardial Dysfunction Following Bupropion Overdose: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Bupropion overdose is associated with significant morbidity and mortality due to severe neurologic and cardiovascular toxicity, including seizures and life-threatening arrhythmias. Early recognition of electrocardiographic, clinical, and echocardiographic abnormalities is critical for prompt intervention and prevention of clinical deterioration. We present a case of a 21-year-old female who presented to the emergency department following an intentional polysubstance overdose involving suspected bupropion ingestion. The initial electrocardiogram (EKG) demonstrated sinus tachycardia. However, during continued monitoring, the patient developed QRS widening and seizures. Treatment included benzodiazepines, calcium, and sodium bicarbonate. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) revealed a reduced ejection fraction (EF) of less than 30%, which was later confirmed on formal transthoracic echocardiography. These findings prompted escalation of care, intubation for airway protection and deep sedation, and transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU). During admission, she developed torsades de pointes (TdP), resulting in cardiac arrest. Despite her critical presentation, repeat echocardiography upon resolution of overdose toxicity demonstrated recovery of left ventricular systolic function, with improvement of EF to 50-55% during hospitalization. This case demonstrates the potential role of POCUS in the early recognition of myocardial dysfunction associated with bupropion toxicity. Together with serial EKG monitoring, these findings identified a patient at high risk for clinical deterioration and supported early escalation of care.

papers.title: Association between immediate and early seizures and pre-injury alcohol and marijuana use: A traumatic brain injury model systems national database analysis.
papers.abstract: This study examined the role that pre-injury alcohol and marijuana use have on the incidence of post-traumatic seizures, as well as their relationship with their known risk factors. We hypothesized that pre-injury alcohol and marijuana use would independently predict post-traumatic seizures at 3 separate time points, categorized as immediate, early, and both immediate and early seizures. 3,875 participants were identified using the Traumatic Brain Injury Model Systems National Database. The primary outcome was the occurrence of a post-traumatic seizure. The primary exposure variables of interest included pre-injury alcohol and marijuana use. Covariates included presence of pre-injury seizures, age and sex at injury, and injury-related characteristics. The relationship between pre-injury alcohol and marijuana use, and each seizure outcome was examined using separate logistic regression models, with results reported as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. From the total number of participants 88.8% did not experience seizures, with immediate seizures observed in 269 participants, early seizures observed in 111 participants, and both immediate and early seizures observed in 53 participants. For the immediate seizure group pre-injury alcohol use was not significantly associated with immediate seizures. In the early seizure group, however, alcohol use in the month prior to injury was significantly associated with increased odds, while pre-injury marijuana use was associated with decreased odds. In the combined immediate and early group, alcohol use was not significantly associated, but pre-injury marijuana use was associated with an increased odds of seizure. This study illustrated a possible priming effect of pre-injury alcohol use on post-injury brains, showing a stronger association between the development of early compared to immediate seizures. The effect of marijuana on seizure risk was less clear, nevertheless reinforcing the importance of strong counseling for this vulnerable population, particularly for those with a pre-morbid history of alcohol/substance use.

papers.title: Corpora amylacea and synaptic organization in the human brain analyzed by volume electron microscopy.
papers.abstract: The presence of corpora amylacea in the brain is a frequent finding in normal aging and in a broad spectrum of neurological disorders, yet the significance of these deposits for the organization of human cortical circuits remains unclear. Here, we combined complementary light and electron microscopy approaches to analyze temporal lobe epilepsy biopsy specimens with and without corpora amylacea. Samples containing corpora amylacea showed marked alterations in synaptic circuit microorganization, which were not restricted to areas of corpora amylacea accumulation but extended throughout the cortical tissue. These changes were characterized by neuronal loss, gliosis, reduced synaptic density, an increased proportion of inhibitory synapses, and larger synapses. Integration of these structural findings with clinical data from the same patients further supports the view that corpora amylacea are associated with disease-related pathological processes. Together, these findings provide a basis for understanding the potential significance of corpora amylacea in human brain circuit dysfunction and may help to inform future research studies focusing on disease mechanisms.

papers.title: EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma with leptomeningeal metastasis after osimertinib treatment: intrathecal chemotherapy combined with targeted therapy supported by cerebrospinal fluid next generation sequencing - a case report.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a severe complication of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Conventional cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology has limited sensitivity and often delays diagnosis. We report a case of LM molecularly supported by CSF next-generation sequencing (NGS) after three negative cytological examinations. NGS also revealed a potential bypass resistance alteration that informed subsequent treatment considerations.
CASE: A 57-year-old female never-smoker had EGFR exon 21 p.L858R-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. After 18 months of first-line osimertinib (80 mg once daily), she developed progressive nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. Contrast-enhanced cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed linear leptomeningeal enhancement. Lumbar puncture showed markedly elevated intracranial pressure (>300 mmH2O) and increased CSF protein. However, three CSF cytological examinations (including cell block sections) found no malignant cells. CSF NGS detected the EGFR p.L858R mutation identical to the primary tumor, together with CDK4 amplification. Integrated with the clinical and MRI presentation, these findings supported a diagnosis of probable LM and suggested cell-cycle bypass activation as a potential mechanism associated with osimertinib resistance. After intrathecal methotrexate plus continued oral osimertinib, her neurological symptoms improved markedly, and intracranial pressure returned to normal. The first seizure occurred on March 19, 2026, and MRI on April 8, 2026 confirmed new brain parenchymal metastases. Whole-brain radiotherapy with a local boost to the metastases, antiepileptic treatment, and continued osimertinib led to obvious shrinkage of the intracranial lesions. Grade 3 thrombocytopenia and severe malnutrition occurred during multimodal therapy and improved with supportive care. At the last follow-up, the patient was clinically stable with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) of 1.
CONCLUSIONS: CSF NGS can overcome the diagnostic bottleneck of cytology-negative LM. It can also identify potential resistance alterations and actionable targets (such as CDK4/6 inhibitors) at the same time, providing direction for subsequent targeted strategies. As part of multimodal therapy, intrathecal chemotherapy combined with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) can contribute to disease control in the CSF compartment, whereas parenchymal progression still requires salvage radiotherapy. Cumulative hematological and nutritional toxicity should be monitored during sequential multimodal therapy.

papers.title: Twenty Years of the Concept of the Privileged Extracellular Region: From Early Computations to Modern Anatomical Evidence.
papers.abstract: The brain extracellular space (ECS) is a heterogeneous and plastic compartment. The concept of the privileged extracellular region (PER) was introduced in 2004 as a computationally derived, spatially restricted microdomain of the ECS immediately surrounding glial cells, within which potassium (K+) accumulates preferentially and independently from the broader extracellular milieu. Using mathematical modeling of membrane currents in astrocytes and oligodendrocytes, the seminal paper demonstrated that the volume of the ECS accessible for K+ accumulation during depolarization was 10-100-fold smaller around oligodendrocytes than around astrocytes, establishing the first quantitative evidence for spatial heterogeneity of the periglial ECS. Over the following two decades, converging lines of structural, functional, and clinical evidence have dramatically expanded this concept. Perisynaptic astrocytic regions and extracellular geometry have now been visualized at nanoscale resolution using STED, dSTORM, and super-resolution shadow imaging (SUSHI), revealing a spongiform architecture with fine leaflets and reflexive loops that delineate functionally distinct microdomains at the synaptic interface. EAAT2/GLT-1 glutamate transporters and Kir4.1 K+ channels concentrated within these processes provide the molecular infrastructure for localized neurotransmitter clearance and K+ siphoning. Disruption of PER geometry-through reactive gliosis, astrocytic atrophy during aging, or leaflet retraction-contributes to the pathophysiology of epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease, ischemia, and cognitive decline. The present review traces the intellectual lineage of the PER concept, integrates two decades of anatomical and functional evidence, and highlights the therapeutic implications of understanding periglial microdomains as active regulators of brain homeostasis.

papers.title: When elimination leaves patients behind: clinical, serologic and molecular evidence of a human African trypanosomiasis case highlighting diagnostic, surveillance and treatment gaps in Nigeria.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite substantial progress toward elimination, human African trypanosomiasis (HAT) remains vulnerable to under-recognition in low-surveillance settings. Nigeria, historically endemic for HAT, has reported very few recent cases, which raises questions about whether declining incidence reflects true interruption of transmission or limitations in surveillance and diagnostic systems. Here, we report a case that illustrates the unique challenges of case detection and surveillance, confirmation and treatment in Nigeria, which resulted in poor patient outcomes and ongoing transmission that may hinder sustainable HAT elimination.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 17-year-old male from Imo State, Nigeria, first developed recurrent seizures in 2020 at the age of 12 and received treatment for epilepsy for approximately 4 years before progressive neurological deterioration prompted further investigations for HAT. Serological and molecular testing supported infection with Trypanosoma brucei, and cerebrospinal fluid findings were consistent with second-stage HAT. Tested family members also showed positive serological and molecular results, suggesting possible undetected transmission within the household. Despite the cumulative clinical, serologic and molecular evidence, treatment was not initiated owing to prevailing operational practices in the country. Patient's symptoms remain unabated with continued anti-epilepsy treatment and no access to HAT medications.
CONCLUSIONS: This case demonstrates how prolonged clinical misdiagnosis, gaps in surveillance, and barriers to accessing treatment can delay recognition and management of HAT in low-prevalence settings, especially in the absence of parasitological confirmation. It also highlights broader challenges facing elimination programmes, illustrating how the gap between international diagnostic/treatment guidelines and operational practice affects patient care. The detection of infection markers among family members further raises concern about under-recognized transmissions in Nigeria. Strengthening clinician awareness, enhancing surveillance systems, conducting family-based case investigations, and ensuring timely access to adequate diagnosis and treatment will be essential for achieving equitable HAT elimination.

papers.title: Clinical spectrum of intracellular cobalamin metabolism disorders: a single-center retrospective study from the United Arab Emirates.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cobalamin is essential for DNA synthesis and for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and methionine synthase activity. Inherited disorders of intracellular cobalamin (Cbl) metabolism are single-gene defects affecting absorption, transport, or intracellular processing, with variable phenotypes depending on the severity and location of the defect. Data from high consanguinity populations, such as the UAE, are limited.
AIM: To describe the clinical, biochemical, and molecular characteristics of patients with intracellular Cbl metabolism disorders at Tawam Hospital, UAE.
METHODS: Retrospective review of patients followed between January 2010 and December 2025. Data included demographics, clinical features, laboratory and radiological findings, molecular results, treatment, and outcomes.
RESULTS: Twelve patients were identified: 8 CblC, 1 CblE, 1 CblG, and 2 unclassified. Consanguinity was present in 75%. The earliest diagnosis was at 8 days; 91.6% were symptomatic. Presentations included seizures (58%), apparent life-threatening events (33%), hydrocephalus and cytopenia (25% each), global developmental delay, osteoporosis, hypothyroidism, hypogonadism, multicystic kidney, and psychiatric symptoms. Homocysteine was elevated in all. The MMACHC c.271dupA variant was common; a novel variant in the MTRR gene was identified. All received parenteral hydroxocobalamin, betaine, and carnitine with partial biochemical improvement. The newborn-screened patient had a favorable outcome.
CONCLUSION: This cohort broadens the phenotypic spectrum to endocrine, renal, and psychiatric manifestations. Early diagnosis and hydroxocobalamin treatment improve outcomes, though neurocognitive and ophthalmologic complications persist.

papers.title: Glymphatic system dysfunction in anti-NMDAR encephalitis: a comparative DTI-ALPS study with healthy controls and epilepsy patients.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis is characterized by pathogenic autoantibody-mediated synaptic dysfunction, yet the mechanisms facilitating antibody access to the brain parenchyma remain incompletely understood. The glymphatic system, which supports cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange along perivascular spaces, has been implicated in immune surveillance and waste clearance; however, its involvement in anti-NMDAR encephalitis has not been fully investigated in vivo.
METHODS: Glymphatic system-related function was assessed using diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) in 15 patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis, 17 patients with epilepsy, and 18 healthy controls. Group differences in ALPS-index values were analyzed with adjustment for age and sex. Associations between ALPS-indexes, clinical severity, and regional brain volumes were further examined.
RESULTS: ALPS-index values were significantly reduced in both anti-NMDAR encephalitis and epilepsy compared with healthy controls. Across all groups, ALPS-indexes demonstrated strong bilateral correlations, with consistently lower values in the right hemisphere. In anti-NMDAR encephalitis, lower ALPS-index values were associated with longer hospitalization and higher modified Rankin Scale scores, whereas no associations were observed with cerebrospinal fluid anti-NMDAR antibody titers. In epilepsy, ALPS-indexes showed a distinct pattern of clinical and structural correlations, including associations with regional brain volumes that were absent in the NMDAR group. Receiver operating characteristic analysis indicated moderate-to-good discriminative performance of ALPS-indexes for both disease groups.
CONCLUSION: DTI-ALPS reveals altered perivascular water diffusivity in anti-NMDAR encephalitis, which correlates with clinical severity independently of antibody titers. These findings suggest glymphatic-related dysfunction in anti-NMDAR encephalitis, and indicate that the ALPS-index captures disease-relevant pathophysiological processes beyond antibody burden, with potential utility as a noninvasive imaging marker for clinical assessment and prognosis in immune-mediated encephalitis.

papers.title: Ephaptic coupling between neurons: a systematic review of mathematical models.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ephaptic coupling is a relatively underexplored mechanism of neuronal interaction mediated by perturbations of the extracellular electric potential without the formation of conventional chemical or electrical synapses. Although the first theoretical accounts of ephaptic interactions appeared as early as the 1940s, computational approaches to this phenomenon have been actively developed only since the late 1990s and early 2000s, based on classical models of neuronal activity and cable theory. Both simplified phenomenological and biophysically detailed models have been developed. The former capture only essential features of large-scale neuronal dynamics and offer high computational efficiency, whereas the latter incorporate more complex characteristics, such as the properties of myelinated and unmyelinated fibers, the spatial distribution of nodes of Ranvier, axonal diameter heterogeneity, and the dynamics of extracellular ion concentrations. Recent studies highlight a growing interest in ephaptic interactions, particularly in their potential roles in neuronal synchronization, sensory coding, the propagation of epileptic seizures, and the development of neurodegenerative as well as demyelinating disorders.
OBJECTIVE AND METHODS: This work presents the systematic review dedicated to mathematical models of ephaptic coupling. The review aims to consolidate the diverse computational approaches used to study ephaptic coupling and to outline the main mechanisms of this phenomenon explored in modeling studies. The reviewed models were classified by type, tested hypotheses, and availability of open-source implementations.
RESULTS: We surveyed nearly seventy mathematical models of ephaptic coupling. The review highlights how ephaptic interactions may contribute not only to normal brain function-such as synchronization and sensory processing-but also to pathological conditions, including epilepsy, demyelination, neuropathic pain, and neurodegeneration. By bringing together disparate studies, we aim to make the modeling of ephaptic coupling comprehensible to a broad scientific audience, including researchers with little prior experience in this area, stimulate further integration of computational and experimental approaches, and promote investigation of ephaptic mechanisms in both health and disease.
CONCLUSION: This review serves both as a reference point for researchers developing new computational models and as a resource for those seeking to understand how ephaptic interactions may shape neuronal dynamics.

papers.title: Development and Validation of an Early Clinical Prediction Model for Post-Encephalitic Epilepsy in Children With Viral Encephalitis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Post-encephalitic epilepsy (PEE) is a serious long-term sequela of pediatric viral encephalitis, yet early risk stratification tools are lacking. In this single-center retrospective cohort study of 206 children with viral encephalitis, 43 (20.87%) developed PEE during follow-up. A multivariable logistic regression model incorporating 4 early clinical predictors-acute seizure count, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) white blood cell count, consciousness disturbance, and cortical involvement-demonstrated good discrimination and acceptable calibration. Decision curve analysis showed higher net benefit than treat-all and treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.06 to 0.99. Sensitivity analyses, including false-discovery rate correction, adjustment for follow-up duration, pathogen-stratified analyses, and a time-to-event (Cox) model, did not materially alter the principal findings. This model, built from routinely available variables, showed promise for early identification of children at elevated risk for PEE in internal validation. External validation in independent multicenter cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

papers.title: On-Premises Open-Weight Large Language Models for Classifying Epilepsy Brain MRI Reports: A Retrospective Study.
papers.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
papers.abstract: Free-text reports limit the use of imaging data for research cohort screening. This study evaluated whether locally deployed open-weight large language models (LLMs) can classify brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reports in epilepsy without external data transfer, and which forms of domain knowledge improve classification. In this single-center retrospective study, 1210 epilepsy-protocol brain MRI reports were labeled by a board-certified neuroradiologist for abnormality status and primary imaging finding (eight classes). A held-out test set of 206 reports was classified by a biomedical (OpenBioLLM-8B) and a general-purpose (Qwen3.5-9B) LLM on a single 24-GB graphics processing unit, with and without a rule set and example retrieval, and compared with a fine-tuned radiology-specific BERT model, an independent neuroradiology fellow, and a same-base control model. The primary outcome was the macro-averaged F1 score for the primary finding. Without task-specific training, the general-purpose model achieved a finding macro-F1 of 0.63 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.53-0.70), comparable to the fine-tuned BERT model (0.59; difference, - 0.04; 95% CI, - 0.13 to 0.07) and to inter-reader agreement (0.61; κ = 0.59). A rule set stating institutional category definitions improved the biomedical model (difference, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.11-0.33) without significantly reducing performance in any model, whereas biomedical fine-tuning conferred no advantage over the control model and example retrieval did not help. Residual errors concentrated where the readers disagreed. Locally deployed LLMs performed comparably to inter-reader agreement, which may support human-verified cohort screening; in this institution-specific task, explicit category definitions were more useful than biomedical specialization.

papers.title: Neurological manifestations in pediatric COVID-19: a comparative single-center study.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical characteristics, investigations, management, and outcomes of hospitalized children with SARS-CoV-2 infection with and without neurological involvement, and to determine whether neurological disease reflects systemic severity or a distinct clinical pattern.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of children aged 1 month-16 years with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a tertiary pediatric center between June 2022 and June 2023. Patients were divided into those with neurological manifestations (ND group, n = 24) and those without neurological involvement (non-ND group, n = 23). Demographic features, clinical presentation, laboratory and neuroimaging findings, treatment, and outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: Children with neurological involvement were significantly older (median 5.75 vs. 3.00 years, p = 0.022) and less likely to present with fever or systemic inflammatory features. They demonstrated lower inflammatory markers and significantly less cardiac involvement, including dilated cardiomyopathy. Common neurological presentations included encephalopathy (50%), headache (45.8%), and seizures (20.8%). 37% met MIS-C criteria. Neuroimaging revealed lacunar infarctions, demyelinating white matter lesions, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, and cauda equina nerve root enhancement. Despite similar mortality rates, children with neurological involvement had a significantly higher rate of incomplete recovery, with more than a quarter experiencing persistent neurological sequelae (29.2% vs. 4.3%, p = 0.048).
CONCLUSION: Neurological manifestations of pediatric COVID-19 represent a clinically distinct pattern characterized by limited systemic inflammation but an increased risk of persistent neurological sequelae. Early neurological evaluation, appropriate neuroimaging, and structured long-term follow-up are warranted even in the absence of severe systemic illness.

papers.title: IMPACT: an open-source workflow for unified variant interpretation using phenotype-driven filtering.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive interpretation of whole-genome sequencing data for phenotypes with complex genetic architecture requires integrating diverse variant classes, but most workflows remain focused on single-nucleotide changes and small indels. We present IMPACT, an open-source, phenotype-configurable pipeline that harmonizes preprocessing, applies variant-specific annotation, and consolidates single-nucleotide variants, indels, structural variants, and copy-number variants within an interactive R Shiny interface. Applied to the UK Biobank cohorts with deafness (n = 126) and epilepsy (n = 41), IMPACT prioritized 565 and 126 variants, respectively. Of these, 512 and 103 were non-incidental, phenotype-relevant candidates, which were subsequently reviewed using ACMG-aligned evidence and classified as pathogenic or candidate variants of uncertain significance where supported. All deafness participants and 87.8% of epilepsy participants carried at least one candidate variant, with configurations ranging from single high-impact variants to compound heterozygotes spanning variant classes. By coupling phenotype-aware filtering with cross-type visualization, IMPACT addresses critical gaps in genome interpretation and offers a scalable foundation for research-driven curation and precision medicine.

papers.title: Differential Expression and Therapeutic Targeting of K+ Channels in Neurological Disorders: An Integrative Approach.
papers.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
papers.abstract: Potassium (K+) channels regulate cellular homeostasis and electrical signaling, particularly in the nervous system, and their dysfunction is linked to neurological disorders such as epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease (AD), and Parkinson's disease (PD). In this study, Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets (GSE252132, GSE190451, and GSE160299) were analyzed using GEO2R to identify differentially expressed K+ channel genes. A total of 2741, 3681, and 861 differentially expressed genes were identified in AD, epilepsy, and PD, respectively, including the common K+ channel genes KCNJ5, KCNJ6, and KCNJ12. Functional enrichment using Enrichr highlighted potassium ion transport, potassium channel complexes, voltage-gated potassium channel activity, and gonadotropin-releasing hormone secretion. STRING and Cytoscape-based protein-protein interaction and Molecular Complex Detection analyses identified 13 hub genes, including KCNJ6, KCNJ5, and KCNJ12. miRNet analysis identified 12 miRNAs, 1 transcription factor, and 7 target genes, with hsa-miR-138-5p predicted to regulate KCNJ6. Virtual screening of 2315 Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs and 2390 Traditional Chinese Medicine compounds identified Sorafenib, Hinokiflavone, Posaconazole, and 1,3,6-Tri-O-galloyl-beta-D-glucose as promising KCNJ6-binding candidates. These findings highlight K+ channels, particularly KCNJ6, as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in neurological disorders.

papers.title: [Genetic and phenotypic profiling of children with Global developmental delay/Intellectual disability associated with chromosomal copy number variations].
papers.journal: Zhonghua yi xue yi chuan xue za zhi = Zhonghua yixue yichuanxue zazhi = Chinese journal of medical genetics
papers.iso_journal: Zhonghua Yi Xue Yi Chuan Xue Za Zhi
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the clinical characteristics of children with Global developmental delay/Intellectual disability (GDD/ID) due to chromosomal copy number variants (CNVs), and to explore the pathogenic mechanisms of CNVs.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 24 children diagnosed with GDD/ID at the Department of Pediatrics, Hebei General Hospital from June 2021 to June 2024. All children underwent whole genome copy number variation sequencing (CNV-seq) and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA). Clinical features, CNVs types, and pathogenicity were analyzed. This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the hospital [Ethics No.: (2022) Research Ethics Review No. 168].
RESULTS: Among the 24 children with GDD/ID, 15 (62.50%) had seizures, 6 (25.00%) had autism spectrum disorder (ASD), 14 (58.33%) had language developmental delay, 3 (12.50%) had attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), 14 (58.33%) had dysmorphic facial features, 4 (16.67%) had visual or auditory impairment, 11 (45.83%) had concomitant abnormalities, and 10 (41.67%) had abnormal cranial imaging findings. Pathogenic CNVs were detected in 22 of of them. In 20 of these cases, the CNVs were consistent with entries in the OMIM database or previously reported GDD/ID-related syndromes, while the remaining 2 were variants of uncertain significance.
CONCLUSION: Children with CNVs-related GDD/ID exhibit complex multi-system phenotypes and frequently present with co-morbid neurodevelopmental disorders. For children with GDD/ID and complex phenotypes, CNVs should be considered as a primary etiology. Follow-up management should be strengthened, and systematic genetic counseling should be provided to their families.

papers.title: Intracranial Subdural Empyema Associated with Streptococcus Dysgalactiae Subsp. Equisimilis in a Patient with Chronic Subdural Hematomas.
papers.abstract: A 73-year-old man with conservatively managed bilateral chronic subdural hematomas presented with fever and vomiting, followed by a seizure and impaired consciousness. Craniotomy revealed subdural pus, supporting intracranial subdural empyema arising in these hematomas. Streptococcus dysgalactiae subsp. equisimilis (SDSE) was recovered from blood and subdural cultures, although a polymicrobial infection could not be excluded because subdural sampling followed antibiotic initiation. He improved after drainage and four weeks of antibiotic treatment. SDSE bacteremia with neurological deterioration should prompt consideration of subdural empyema. Hematogenous seeding was considered to be the most likely route of infection.

papers.title: Psychosis in medically ill Children and Adolescents.
papers.journal: Child and adolescent psychiatric clinics of North America
papers.iso_journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
papers.abstract: Psychosis in children and adolescents caused by medical illnesses/conditions is rare. Visual hallucinations, confusion, and change of baseline mentation support this diagnosis. Certain physical examination findings also suggest a secondary etiology of psychosis. Specific laboratory, imaging, and other tests are then utilized. Numerous medical etiologies have been identified to cause psychosis in children and adolescents, specifically delirium, inborn errors of metabolism, genetic syndromes, encephalitides, other systemic infections, space occupying lesions, seizures, trauma, and endocrine and nutritional disorders. Treatment is mainly extrapolated from the delirium literature, and there are conflicting data showing the utility of antipsychotic use for secondary psychosis.

papers.title: Diagnosis and genetic analysis of a case of glycosylphosphatidylinositol biosynthesis deficiency 15 caused by compound heterozygous mutations of GPAA1.
papers.abstract: Glycosylphosphatidylinositol biosynthesis deficiency 15 (GPIBD15, MIM: 617810) is an autosomal recessive inherited metabolic disorder caused by mutations in the GPAA1 gene. It is primarily characterized by global developmental delay, intellectual disability, early-onset epileptic seizures, hypotonia, and cerebellar atrophy. In this study, we reported a child diagnosed with GPIBD15 whose main clinical manifestations included dysplasia and cerebral dysfunction. We performed whole-exome sequencing on the patient and his parents. The patient was found to harbor compound heterozygous mutations c.1288C>T(p.P430S) and c.1621C>T(p.R541W) in the GPAA1 gene. The c.1288C>T(p.P430S) variant was inherited from the father, while the c.1621C>T(p.R541W) variant was inherited from the mother. Pathogenicity prediction, evolutionary conservation analysis and protein structure prediction analysis of these mutation sites showed that the variants are deleterious and located at highly conserved residues. These mutations lead to obvious changes in the secondary and tertiary structures of the protein, suggesting that they may affect protein function. To further investigate their functional impact, we constructed plasmid expression vectors harboring the c.1288C>T(p.P430S) and c.1621C> T(p.R541W) mutations and transfected them into HEK293T cells. We observed that co-transfection of the two mutant constructs significantly increased GPAA1 mRNA expression levels, while the corresponding protein expression levels were markedly decreased. Subcellular localization analysis showed no apparent difference between the wild-type and mutant proteins. In conclusion, we report a case of GPIBD15 caused by two novel compound heterozygous mutations in the GPAA1 gene. The pathogenic mechanism may be associated with mutation-induced structural alterations and reduced protein expression. Our findings expand the mutational spectrum of GPAA1 and provide valuable insights for early diagnosis and genetic counseling of patients with GPIBD15.

papers.title: Dravet syndrome: clinical features across the lifespan, molecular findings, and therapeutic approaches.
papers.abstract: Dravet syndrome is a prototypical genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, caused by pathogenic variants in the sodium channel alpha-1 subunit gene (SCN1A) in 95% of individuals. The classic presentation of Dravet syndrome is a baby aged about 6 months, with typical development, who presents with a prolonged febrile generalised tonic-clonic or hemiclonic seizure, and frequent seizures ensue. Individuals with Dravet syndrome usually develop multiple seizure types alongside developmental slowing, and sometimes regression, and a range of morbidities emerge. Dravet syndrome is associated with a poor prognosis and a high risk of mortality. De novo SCN1A pathogenic variants typically cause Dravet syndrome, but parental mosaicism might occur, with implications for reproductive counselling. Early diagnosis is essential to guide prompt, optimal selection of antiseizure medications to control seizures and improve long-term outcomes. Natural history studies are crucial for interpreting the outcomes of trials of novel therapies. Newer antiseizure medications show improved efficacy in controlling seizures, often associated with developmental gains. Pivotal antisense oligonucleotide and genetic therapy trials show promise to transform this devastating disease.

papers.title: Epigenetic control of neural homeostasis by REST.
papers.abstract: Neural network stability relies on homeostatic plasticity mechanisms acting across intrinsic, synaptic, and glial levels to counter persistent deviations in activity. In hyperexcitable or chronically stressed brain states, including epilepsy, neuroinflammation, ageing, and early Alzheimer's disease, sustained stress can destabilize these compensatory programs and network function. Alongside its established roles in neuronal differentiation and neurological disease when dysregulated, repressor element-1 silencing transcription (REST), also known as neuron-restrictive silencer factor (NRSF) is emerging as a multilevel, long-timescale epigenetic hub linking neuronal activity to coordinated homeostatic transcriptional programs. This review examines this less explored homeostatic dimension of REST biology. Rather than acting as a binary repressor, REST functions as a tunable chromatin-regulatory platform whose output depends on RE1 architecture, chromatin context, cellular state, and activation dynamics. We discuss how REST-dependent programs regulate intrinsic homeostasis, excitatory and inhibitory synaptic scaling, and astrocyte-mediated homeostatic support. Finally, we propose that neuronal energy metabolism may bias REST signaling toward adaptive compensation rather than maladaptive repression.

papers.title: Beyond sensitivity: Performance, methodological heterogeneity, and real-time translation of wrist-worn convulsive seizure detection devices - A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Wrist-worn seizure-detection devices can detect convulsive seizures, but pooled performance estimates may obscure methodological differences between studies. We evaluated the performance, heterogeneity, and translational readiness of wrist-worn non-EEG systems for automated detection of convulsive and generalized tonic-clonic (GTC) seizures. We systematically searched MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Event-level sensitivity for convulsive and GTC seizures was pooled using random-effects generalized linear mixed models; false-alarm rates (FARs) were pooled as incidence rates per 24 h. We evaluated heterogeneity, prespecified subgroups, methodological variability, detection latency, and progression to real-time intervention. Twenty studies comprising 1598 participants and 71,310 monitoring hours were included. Pooled random-effects sensitivity was approximately 93% for convulsive seizures and 96% for GTC seizures, with heterogeneity exceeding 75% for both outcomes. The pooled FAR was approximately 0.39/24 h, with heterogeneity approaching 99%. Neither sensing modality, study phase, population, algorithm locking, nor offline versus real-time processing explained performance differences under random-effects modeling. Methodological variability extended to seizure eligibility, amplitude and duration thresholds, temporal windowing, classifier architecture, operating-point selection, validation strategy, and FAR denominator construction. Mean detection latency was 30.04 s across nine reporting studies. Only one study directly evaluated translation from detection to real-time caregiver notification and intervention. Wrist-worn devices demonstrate high sensitivity for convulsive and GTC seizure detection, but performance is not yet methodologically uniform or consistently generalizable. Standardized evaluation and independent validation are needed, with future studies extending beyond detection accuracy to reliable real-time alert delivery and actionable intervention.

papers.title: Intranasal dexmedetomidine sedation in pediatric electroencephalography: dose optimization, safety, and EEG characteristics.
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of intranasal dexmedetomidine (DEX) for sedation during pediatric EEG and to explore whether EEG spectral characteristics under DEX differ from those under chloral hydrate.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 224 children (0-18 years) who underwent EEG under intranasal DEX sedation at a single tertiary center (January 2024-April 2025) were analyzed. Patients were stratified into weight-based dosing (Group 1, <50 kg; median 2 μg/kg) and fixed dosing (Group 2, ≥50 kg; median 100 μg). Sedation success, onset time, total sedation time, and adverse events were assessed. In a within-subject subgroup of 11 patients with a prior chloral hydrate EEG, relative power spectral density (rPSD) in the delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands during N1 and N2 sleep was compared using patient-level paired analyses, with mean paired differences, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and correction for multiple comparisons.
RESULTS: Initial sedation success was 94.6% in Group 1 and 94.7% in Group 2; all patients achieved adequate sedation after rescue dosing. Median onset time was 10 minutes in both groups. Adverse events were mild and self-limited (3.2% and 2.6%). No statistically significant differences in rPSD between DEX and chloral hydrate were detected in either sleep stage after correction for multiple comparisons; however, the CIs were wide, and equivalence could not be established. Interictal epileptiform discharges were visually unchanged.
CONCLUSION: Intranasal DEX is an effective, well-tolerated sedative for pediatric EEG, and a weight-stratified dosing strategy appears practical. In a small paired subgroup, no significant spectral differences from chloral hydrate were detected; these preliminary quantitative findings warrant confirmation in larger studies.

papers.title: Perceived stigma, social support, and associated factors among adults with epilepsy: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is frequently associated with perceived stigma and inadequate social support, both of which adversely affect patients' psychosocial well-being and quality of life. This study aimed to investigate perceived stigma, perceived social support, the relationship between these variables, and factors associated with both among adults with epilepsy. A descriptive, cross-sectional, correlational study was conducted with 147 adults diagnosed with epilepsy who attended the Neurology Outpatient Clinic of Harran University Hospital between June 2025-June 2026. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Perceived Stigma Scale, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. The mean perceived stigma score was 26.58 ± 9.34, while the mean total perceived social support score was 51.91 ± 18.87. Higher perceived stigma was significantly associated with lower educational level, unemployment, work impairment due to epilepsy, lower income, the presence of another chronic disease, concealing the epilepsy diagnosis, and perceiving that others avoided them because of epilepsy (p < 0.05). Higher educational level and not perceiving social rejection were associated with greater perceived social support (p < 0.05). Perceived stigma demonstrated a significant weak negative correlation with total perceived social support (r = -0.405, p = 0.001). These findings highlight the importance of considering stigma and social support in the psychosocial care of people with epilepsy. Healthcare professionals should assess these needs and facilitate access to appropriate psychosocial resources, including peer support and self-management programmes. In addition, public education initiatives and targeted support programmes may help address misconceptions about epilepsy, reduce stigma, and enhance social acceptance.

papers.title: Towards a national drug checking database to monitor the drug supply and prevent drug-related harms: A narrative review.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The changing drug supply poses challenges for preventing drug-related harms. Timely drug supply information is critical for public health and clinical responses, yet existing surveillance systems lack the nuance and speed to detect emerging trends. Drug checking services may help address these gaps by enhancing monitoring of drug supplies, informing public health and clinical interventions, and supporting evidence-based policymaking. This review examines the evolution of drug checking in the United States, evaluates the strengths and limitations of these data relative to existing surveillance systems, and provides recommendations for integrating drug checking into national drug surveillance efforts.
METHODS: We conducted a narrative review to synthesize the current evidence on drug checking with an emphasis on the U.S.
CONTEXT: Findings from published studies were supplemented by the expertise of subject matter experts actively engaged in drug checking research, practice, and policy.
RESULTS: Compared to traditional drug surveillance, drug checking data offer several advantages, including face validity (representing drugs at the level of consumption rather than from upstream seizures), timeliness (days to weeks rather than months to years), breadth (inclusion of novel psychoactive substances) and depth (inclusion of contextual cues). Four recommendations emerged from the review: expanding sustainable funding; advancing drug checking technologies; strengthening legal protections for programs and clients; and establishing data governance and stewardship frameworks to support data sharing, quality, and privacy.
CONCLUSIONS: Greater investment in drug checking services, supported by coordinated data systems and enabling policies, could strengthen surveillance and advance efforts to prevent and reduce drug-related harms.

papers.title: Preferential responses to spectrally degraded sentences in the human cortex revealed by intracranial electrophysiology.
papers.abstract: Despite progress in cochlear implant (CI) technology, there is considerable variability in outcomes, in part attributed to the function of central auditory pathways. Spectrally degraded sounds presented to normal-hearing listeners can be used to approximate cortical sound processing by CI users. Prior intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) work identified "clear-preferred" and less common "vocoded-preferred" differential responses to clear and noise-vocoded non-word speech tokens. Better identification of vocoded consonants was associated with activation of the cortical dorsal auditory stream. The present study further characterized these differential responses using sentence stimuli that are expected to engage the ventral processing stream. Participants were neurosurgical epilepsy patients undergoing iEEG monitoring. Sentences were degraded using a 3-band noise vocoder. Analysis of iEEG data focused on event-related band power (ERBP) between 4-150 Hz. Differential responses (ERBP augmentation or suppression) to clear and vocoded sentences were observed both in early and late portions of the sentence, suggesting a sustained, rather than transient, nature of the preferential responses. Clear-preferred responses are likely driven by spectral complexity and intelligibility. Vocoded-preferred responses may reflect increased processing demands associated with challenging listening conditions. These responses occurred primarily in core auditory cortex and regions along the dorsal auditory stream but were virtually absent in prefrontal cortex. Identifying regions involved in the processing of degraded speech has potential clinical utility and may present candidate targets for neuromodulation-based CI rehabilitation strategies.

papers.title: Association of epilepsy subtypes with elevated depressive symptoms in children.
papers.journal: Archives de pediatrie : organe officiel de la Societe francaise de pediatrie
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to determine the coexistence of elevated depressive symptoms and epilepsy in children and adolescents and to ascertain if the symptoms are related to a specific localization.
METHODS: Patients between ages 9-14 with temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), extratemporal lobe epilepsy (ETLE), and generalized epilepsy were followed up, and healthy siblings of these patients in the same age group as the control group were included in the study. The study included 89 epilepsy patients and 89 control subjects. Children's Depression Inventory (CDI) was used to determine the rate of elevated depressive symptoms.
RESULTS: The average age of the patients was 12.2 ± 1.8, 50.6% of them were female. Fifty (56.2%) of the patients were being followed up for generalized epilepsy, 14 (15.7%) for ETLE, and 25 (28.1%) for TLE. Elevated depressive symptoms (CDI ≥19) were found to be significantly higher in the TLE and ETLE epilepsy groups compared to the control group (p < 0.001 and p = 0.004, respectively). The rate of elevated depressive symptoms (CDI ≥19) was significantly higher in the TLE group compared to the generalized epilepsy group (52.0%vs. 12.0%, p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed between TLE and ETLE, or between ETLE and the generalized epilepsy group (both p > 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression analysis showed that TLE remained independently associated with elevated depressive symptoms (adjusted OR 7.87, 95% CI 2.42-25.64; p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated depressive symptoms in children and adolescent patients were more frequently detected in the TLE group. Prospective multicenter studies are warranted to clarify the relationship between epileptic focus localization and elevated depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Reversible Rapidly Progressive Dementia Associated With ASIA Syndrome Secondary to Silicone Implants.
papers.abstract: A 33-year-old woman with a medical history of polycystic ovary syndrome on combined oral contraceptive pills, insulin resistance, and bilateral silicone breast implants (SBIs) placed 10 years prior presented with a 2-month history of intermittent myoclonic jerks involving the head, trunk, and lower limbs; polyarthralgia; and cognitive and functional decline (compared with being previously independent in her activities of daily living). Family history was significant for epilepsy in her mother and 2 brothers. Neurologic examination revealed disorientation, significantly impaired short-term recall, visuospatial memory impairment, and a limited attention span. Her speech was characterized by frequent paraphasic errors and anomia; she also exhibited mild gait ataxia. Diagnostic studies ruled out common autoimmune diseases. Brain MRI and electroencephalography revealed no abnormalities, and CSF analysis was normal. Genetic testing for inherited prion disease and Huntington disease was negative, and serum and urinary copper levels were unremarkable. As part of a paraneoplastic workup, breast MRI revealed intracapsular rupture of both SBIs. The implants were surgically removed with complete capsulectomy. The patient's symptoms resolved completely by the seventh postoperative day. At the 6-month follow-up, she remained asymptomatic and had returned to her baseline functional status. Given the temporal association between implant rupture, explantation, and symptom resolution, the presentation was considered most consistent with a case of reversible rapidly progressive dementia secondary to the autoimmune/inflammatory syndrome induced by adjuvants.

papers.title: Oligonucleotide-mediated AASS silencing as a potential therapeutic strategy for ALDH7A1 deficiency and glutaric aciduria type I.
papers.abstract: α-Aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS) catalyzes the first two steps of lysine catabolism. Inherited metabolic disorders affecting enzymes downstream of AASS, including α-aminoadipic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH7A1) deficiency, which causes pyridoxine-dependent epilepsy, and glutaric aciduria type I, cause accumulation of potentially neurotoxic lysine-derived metabolites. Current therapies incompletely prevent metabolite accumulation and neurological sequelae. We evaluated whether hepatic AASS silencing could reduce conversion of lysine into downstream metabolites. Antisense oligonucleotides and small interfering RNAs targeting AASS reduced disease-associated metabolites in patient-derived cells from individuals with ALDH7A1 deficiency and glutaric aciduria type I. Hepatocyte-selective delivery, enabled by N-acetylgalactosamine conjugation, achieved >90% liver-specific Aass knockdown in wild-type and Aldh7a1 knockout mice, with sustained protein suppression and reduced accumulation of downstream lysine-derived metabolites. These findings support further evaluation of oligonucleotide-mediated AASS silencing, including liver-directed delivery, as a substrate reduction strategy for ALDH7A1 deficiency and glutaric aciduria type I.

papers.title: Duration and intensity of chronic treadmill exercise differentially modulate hippocampal neuronal apoptosis in PTZ-kindled rats.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThe objective of this study was to evaluate how chronic treadmill exercise-varying in intensity and duration-influences hippocampal neuronal apoptosis within a pentylenetetrazol (PTZ)-induced kindling model.MethodsA total of 96 male Wistar rats were divided into eight experimental cohorts: a control group (C), a PTZ-only group (PC), and groups subjected to short-term (SE), moderate (ME), and high-intensity (HE) exercise, both with and without PTZ administration (PSE, PME, and PHE, respectively). Kindling was induced by PTZ (35 mg per kg, i.p., three days per week). The exercise groups were subject to specific treadmill protocols according to their intensity. Neuronal apoptosis in the hippocampus was analysed by immunohistochemistry for Bcl-2, Bax and Caspase-3 and by TUNEL staining.ResultsNo significant statistical difference in anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 or Bax levels was observed between the treatment groups (P>0.05). However, there were significant differences in the scores for Caspase-3 (P <0.001) and TUNEL (P = 0.001). Low-intensity exercise (PSE) did not significantly induce activation of Caspase-3 compared with control. Conversely, moderate (PME) and high (PHE) exercise significantly increased the number of apoptotic cells in the hippocampus. In particular, the PHE group had the highest Caspase-3 activity (10.3 ± 3.61) while the PME group had the highest TUNEL positivity (15.50 ± 22.1).ConclusionsIn this PTZ-induced rat model, hippocampal apoptosis-related markers differed across exercise conditions. Moderate- and high-intensity exercise combined with PTZ were associated with increased Caspase-3 activity and TUNEL positivity, whereas the PSE group showed no detectable Caspase-3 activity. These findings require cautious interpretation because of the experimental animal model and the study's methodological limitations. Further research is needed to clarify the effects of exercise intensity on neuronal apoptosis in epilepsy.

papers.title: Prevalence of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy Without Contact Sport Repetitive Head Impact Exposure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: A pooled baseline prevalence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in populations without repetitive head impact (RHI) exposure is needed to contextualize prevalence in other cohorts.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the pooled prevalence of CTE in populations without documented contact sport-based RHI exposure.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed and Embase were searched from inception through February 23, 2026, using terms for CTE, prevalence, epidemiology, and neuropathology.
STUDY SELECTION: Studies reporting CTE prevalence in cohorts without documented contact sport RHI history were included and classified by ascertainment rigor into a primary group with verified absence of contact sport RHI or a secondary unscreened reference cohort. Studies were excluded for cohort overlap or for RHI-linked comorbid conditions (eg, epilepsy).
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Data were independently extracted by 2 authors, with discrepancy resolved by a third. Risk of bias and quality were assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Pooled prevalence was calculated using a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Heterogeneity (I2 and τ2) and robustness (leave-one-out sensitivity analysis) were assessed.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Confirmed CTE in individuals without documented contact sport RHI history was estimated using pooled prevalence and 95% CIs.
RESULTS: Twelve cohort studies (4421 individuals; weighted mean age at death, 75.1 years; 2481 male [56.1%]) were identified. In the primary analysis of 7 cohorts with verified absence of contact sport RHI (1604 individuals), 12 cases of CTE were identified (crude prevalence, 0.75% [95% CI, 0.43%-1.30%]); pooled prevalence was 1.06% (95% CI, 0.10%-10.79%), reflecting substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 87.0%) and limited precision from few cases and presence of an outlier with 5 of 7 individuals with CTE. Excluding the outlier yielded a pooled prevalence of 0.70% (95% CI, 0.28%-1.74%) and reduced heterogeneity (I2 = 6.6%). In the 5 unscreened reference cohorts (2817 individuals), 17 cases of CTE were identified (crude prevalence, 0.60% [95% CI, 0.38%-0.96%]). Across all 12 cohorts, the crude prevalence was 0.66% (95% CI, 0.46%-0.94%), and the pooled prevalence was 0.85% (95% CI, 0.24%-2.89%).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 cohort studies not selected for contact sport-based RHI exposure found that CTE pathology was rare, with a baseline prevalence of approximately 1%. These findings provide a reference point for interpreting CTE prevalence in other populations, including cohorts with contact sport exposure.

papers.title: Longitudinal quantitative MRI feature analysis in paediatric focal cortical dysplasia: a retrospective longitudinal cohort study.
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) is a common cause of treatment-resistant epilepsy and can be difficult to detect on MRI. Although traditionally considered static, lesion visibility may vary across scans. We assessed whether MELD-derived lesional imaging features differ across serial MRI in histologically confirmed paediatric FCD type II.
METHODS: Twenty-one patients with histopathologically confirmed FCD type II underwent paired T1-weighted MRI; 13 also had paired FLAIR imaging. Images were processed using FastSurfer and a modified MELD feature-extraction pipeline. Lesion-mask feature values were compared with anatomically matched contralateral regions, and time-corrected longitudinal lesion-contralateral differences were calculated. Blinded qualitative neuroradiological review was available for 20/21 subjects.
RESULTS: FCD lesions demonstrated quantitative feature differences from contralateral cortex. In the FLAIR cohort, longitudinal lesion-contralateral differences were consistently positive across sampled grey and white matter depths and remained significant after false discovery rate correction (mean paired differences 0.607-0.737; all pFDR = 0.009). Protocol-restricted FLAIR sensitivity analyses preserved the direction of effect, although restricted subgroups were underpowered. In T1-weighted MRI, longitudinal lesion-contralateral differences were positive across grey matter intensity features, greatest at 75% cortical thickness (mean paired difference 0.185, 95% CI 0.060-0.309, p = 0.006), but no T1 feature survived false discovery rate correction. Neuroradiological review identified possible visually appreciable interval change in a minority of cases, with most apparent change attributed to acquisition-related variation or artefact.
CONCLUSION: Quantitative MRI-derived FCD features can vary across serial paediatric MRI. These findings demonstrate longitudinal imaging feature variability, most consistently in FLAIR-derived measures, with implications for repeat imaging and machine learning derived lesion detection.

papers.title: Influenza A-Associated Encephalitis and Encephalopathy in Adults: An Exploratory Criteria-Based Analysis.
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Influenza A can cause encephalopathy or encephalitis, yet adult data are scarce and the two entities are seldom distinguished systematically. This small retrospective study of five adults explored the feasibility and limitations of classifying these complications with the International Encephalitis Consortium (IEC) 2013 criteria and describes their clinical, radiological, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and treatment characteristics.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed five consecutive adults admitted to a tertiary center with polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed influenza A and acute neurological symptoms, all evaluated with brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), lumbar puncture, and electroencephalography (EEG). Encephalitis was defined by the IEC 2013 criteria (altered mental status > 24 h plus ≥ 2 minor criteria of central nervous system (CNS) inflammation). Data were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Three patients met criteria for encephalitis and two for encephalopathy (four women; age 44-68 years). Respiratory influenza A PCR was positive and CSF PCR negative in all. CSF pleocytosis occurred in two patients, bilateral thalamic and subcortical white matter MRI hyperintensities in two, generalized EEG slowing in four, and focal status epilepticus in one. All received oseltamivir; three received high-dose methylprednisolone, two of whom also required intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange. The categories overlapped substantially: EEG slowing and negative CSF PCR occurred in both, and treatment escalation followed clinical course rather than category, with the most intensive regimen required by one patient in each. At 3 months, three patients were asymptomatic and two, both with encephalitis and structural MRI lesions, had persistent deficits.
CONCLUSION: In this small, hypothesis-generating study, IEC-based classification was feasible, but encephalitis and encephalopathy overlapped substantially and the distinction did not determine treatment. The main contribution lies in illustrating both the feasibility and limitations of criteria-based classification in adults with influenza A, rather than in establishing its clinical utility.

papers.title: Rasmussen's encephalitis in Turner syndrome needing a functional hemispherotomy-coincidence or connection?
papers.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
papers.abstract: Rasmussen's encephalitis (RE) is a rare, chronic, immune-mediated epileptic encephalitis characterized by drug-resistant focal seizures, progressive unilateral cortical dysfunction, and hemispheric atrophy. Turner syndrome (TS), caused by complete or partial monosomy X, is associated with increased autoimmune susceptibility. The coexistence of RE and TS has not, to our knowledge, been previously reported; however, a single case can only raise the question of chance co-occurrence versus a biologically plausible immunogenetic connection. An eight-year-old girl with karyotype-proven TS presented with a two-year history of progressively worsening drug-resistant focal seizures. Serial MRI demonstrated progressive right hemispheric cortical atrophy, most pronounced in the frontal, insular, and mesial temporal regions, with right hemispheric hypoperfusion on arterial spin labelling. Video-EEG confirmed right frontocentral ictal onset without asynchronous contralateral onset. Despite immunotherapy, seizures persisted, and she underwent right functional hemispherotomy with seizure freedom at 8 months follow-up (Engel class I). We believe this to be the first reported coexistence of TS and RE. Although causality cannot be inferred from a single case, the observation supports discussion of X-linked immune dysregulation as a possible susceptibility factor in rare focal neuroinflammatory disease.
