papers.title: Long-term Electroclinical Outcomes After Herpes Simplex Virus Encephalitis: A Single-Center Case Series.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveHerpes simplex virus encephalitis (HSVE) remains an important cause of severe sporadic encephalitis. Electrographic seizures and status epilepticus may be underrecognized during the acute phase, and their relationship with long-term outcome is incompletely defined. We aimed to describe acute EEG abnormalities and long-term seizure and cognitive outcomes in adults with HSVE.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed adults hospitalized with HSVE in the neurology ward or neurological intensive care unit between 2013 and 2022. Demographic and clinical characteristics, MRI findings, routine or continuous video-EEG findings, antiseizure treatments, and long-term outcomes were obtained from electronic health records and the EEG archive.ResultsNine patients (7 men; age range: 30-77 years) were included. Altered mental status was the most frequent presenting feature, and 3 patients had clinical seizures at presentation. MRI abnormalities were bilateral in 4 patients. EEG showed lateralized periodic discharges in 5 patients, electrographic status epilepticus in 4, and electrographic seizures not meeting status criteria in 1. Median follow-up was 8 years (range: 4-13 years). No patient with available follow-up reported recurrent clinical seizures after discharge. Mood and/or cognitive complaints were present in 6 of 8 patients with evaluable long-term clinical data.ConclusionIn this neurologically selected HSVE cohort, electrographic seizures and status epilepticus were frequent despite clinical seizures being documented in only one-third of patients at presentation. Long-term clinical seizure control was favorable under continued antiseizure treatment, whereas cognitive and mood complaints remained common. Larger studies using systematic continuous EEG and standardized neuropsychological assessment are needed.

papers.title: Real-world antiseizure medication prescribing and treatment pathways in a pediatric health care system.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize antiseizure medication (ASM) selection, subsequent ASM prescribing, and treatment pathways among patients with epilepsy receiving care within a pediatric health care system.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective electronic health record study over 17 years. Each unique ASM was counted once per patient, and ASMs were ordered by the date of their first observed prescription. For each observed ASM, we determined whether a subsequent unique ASM was prescribed during available follow-up. Prescription of a third unique ASM was used as a proxy for potential drug-resistant epilepsy.
RESULTS: Among 20 009 patients, 27 ASMs and 3507 treatment pathways were identified. The most common first-observed ASMs were levetiracetam (35.1%), oxcarbazepine (17.2%), and valproic acid (12.3%). From 2010 to 2026, the proportion of first-observed prescriptions for levetiracetam increased from 23.1% to 41.5%. The proportion of all distinct ASMs first recorded for individual patients that were newer-generation ASMs increased from 0% in 2010 to 9.1% in 2026. The proportion of patients without a subsequent ASM ranged from 16.2% to 69.6% across commonly prescribed first-observed ASMs. Overall, 55.6% of patients had one unique ASM recorded, 22.4% had two, and 22.0% had at least three, thereby meeting the study's prescription-based proxy for potential drug-resistant epilepsy. Beyond the most common single- and two-ASM pathways, each remaining pathway accounted for less than 1% of the cohort.
SIGNIFICANCE: Prescribing remained concentrated among established ASMs, although their relative use changed substantially. The proportion of patients without a subsequent ASM varied widely across medications, and treatment pathways beyond first-observed therapy were highly heterogeneous. These findings characterize real-world treatment patterns and identify a need for comparative effectiveness studies of ASM sequencing.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: We examined antiseizure medication prescribing over 17 years among more than 20 000 patients with epilepsy receiving care in a pediatric health care system. More than half had only one medication recorded, whereas 22% had at least three medications; however, the available records could not determine whether these medications failed to control seizures. Levetiracetam became more commonly prescribed, newer medications remained a small proportion of overall use, and medication sequences varied widely after the first observed treatment. These findings highlight the need for better evidence to guide medication selection after initial treatment.

papers.title: Etiology and geographic variation in acute symptomatic seizure management: An international vignette-based survey.
authors: International League Against Epilepsy Acute Symptomatic Seizure Task Force
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute symptomatic seizures (ASyS) account for nearly half of new onset seizures, but evidence guiding management remains limited. We aimed to characterize international variation in ASyS management across common etiologies.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional, vignette-based survey through the International League Against Epilepsy national chapters (February to May 2025). Five etiology-based vignettes assessed clinical and electrographic ASyS scenario after ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury (TBI), meningitis, hyponatremia, and alcohol withdrawal. Respondents who managed neonatal seizures completed a neonatal stroke vignette. We assessed antiseizure medication (ASM) initiation, duration after clinical ASyS, and continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) use. Interrespondent variability was quantified by normalized Shannon entropy (H'). Multivariable generalized estimating equations accounted for repeated responses.
RESULTS: Among 963 respondents (92 countries), 62% recommended ASM initiation in clinical and 61% in electrographic ASyS scenarios. Overall ASM initiation variability was high (H' = .96), highest for alcohol withdrawal (H' = 1.0), followed by stroke (H' > .9), and consistently higher for electrographic than clinical ASyS. Etiology was the strongest driver of ASM initiation. Compared with stroke, ASM initiation odds were higher for TBI (odds ratio [OR] = 2.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 2.2-2.8) and meningitis (OR = 1.9, 95% CI = 1.7-2.2), and lower for hyponatremia (OR = .2, 95% CI = .2-.2) and alcohol withdrawal (OR = .5, 95% CI = .5-.6). Compared with Europe, initiation odds were higher in North America (OR = 2.7, 95% CI = 2.0-3.6), Asia-Oceania (OR = 2.4, 95% CI = 2.0-3.0), and Latin America (OR = 2.0, 95% CI = 1.5-2.7), but not Africa. These differences persisted after accounting for country income. Compared with stroke, the mean ASM duration was 3.2 months shorter for hyponatremia and .6 months longer for TBI. Alcohol withdrawal durations were polarized (41% discontinued at discharge; 20% continued >12 months). cEEG use was markedly higher in North America than Europe (OR = 11.3, 95% CI = 7.8-16.5). Among 291 neonatal respondents, 75% continued ASM beyond discharge.
SIGNIFICANCE: ASyS management varies markedly, reaching near-maximal heterogeneity in several common scenarios. Although etiology drives decisions, geography and provider characteristics also influence care, underscoring an urgent need for randomized trials and international consensus guidance to harmonize care.

papers.title: Chemical Composition and Anxiolytic Potential of Nectandra grandiflora Essential Oil in Adult Zebrafish (Danio rerio): Behavioral, Molecular Docking, and ADMET Approaches.
papers.abstract: Nectandra grandiflora essential oil was investigated for its chemical composition and neuropharmacological effects in adult zebrafish (Danio rerio), complemented by molecular docking and ADMET predictions. The oil was administered intraperitoneally at 4, 20, and 40 mg/kg (n = 6/group). No evident acute toxicity was observed after 96 h (LD50 >40 mg/kg). In the Light/Dark Test, only 4 mg/kg increased the time spent in the light compartment versus control (p < 0.0001), indicating an anxiolytic-like effect. Flumazenil significantly reduced this response, supporting GABA receptor-mediated neuromodulation. Conversely, none of the tested doses protected against PTZ-induced seizures, differing significantly from diazepam (p < 0.0001). Molecular docking identified SEL as the compound with the most favorable predicted binding affinity to the GABAA receptor, while ADMET analysis suggested potentially favorable pharmacokinetic properties; however, both findings require experimental validation to confirm their biological and pharmacological relevance. Overall, the oil showed anxiolytic-like, but not anticonvulsant, activity under the evaluated conditions.

papers.title: Ketogenic diet therapy in adolescents and adults with epilepsy: A scoping review of cognitive outcomes.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The ketogenic diet treatment (KDT) is an established non-pharmacological treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). However, rigorous research for seizure efficacy based on randomized controlled studies in adolescents and adults remains limited, and cognitive outcomes are rarely assessed using standardized measures.
METHODS: This scoping review has mapped evidence on cognitive outcomes of KDT in adolescents and adults with epilepsy. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, PubMed and Embase were searched for studies published between 1986 and 2026. Eligibility for this review required inclusion of adolescents or adults with epilepsy receiving KDT and reporting cognitive outcomes.
RESULTS: Of 951 records, 19 studies were included. Overall, KDT was associated with favorable seizure and cognitive outcomes, although reports of cognitive outcomes were generally subjective.
SIGNIFICANCE: Rigorous research designs were scarce, and evidence remains limited; future studies should use stronger designs, larger samples, standardized cognitive assessments, and longer follow-up periods.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Research shows that people with epilepsy often experience difficulties with the brain's ability to process information. While dietary treatments have been shown to be effective for seizure control, less is known about their effects on cognition. We reviewed published research examining cognitive outcomes in adolescents and adults with epilepsy following dietary treatment. Most studies suggested that these diets had a positive effect on aspects of cognitive functioning. However, the available evidence remains limited. More studies with better designs using well-established cognitive assessments are needed to better understand these effects.

papers.title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. Biomarkers derived from routine EEG may aid identification of neonates with seizures. We investigated whether scalp high-frequency oscillation (HFO) rates derived from the first eligible routine EEG (1) differentiate neonates with HIE with and without seizures; and (2) contribute to seizure classification alongside established clinical, neurophysiological, and imaging biomarkers.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed routine scalp EEG recordings from 33 term neonates with HIE (17 with seizures, 16 without), obtained at a mean postnatal age of 4 ± 3 days. The mean analyzed EEG duration was 38 ± 14 min in neonates with seizures and 36 ± 20 min in those without. HFO rates in sleep segments were quantified using a validated automated detector.
RESULTS: Scalp HFO rates were significantly higher in neonates with seizures than in those without (.12 ± .11 vs. .03 ± .02 HFOs/min/channel, adjusted p = .02). An HFO rate threshold of .07 HFOs/min/channel optimally discriminated neonates who had seizures from those who did not (area under the curve [AUC] = .81). HFO rates did not differ significantly according to HIE severity, therapeutic hypothermia, antiseizure medication response, EEG background activity, or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities. Multivariable models incorporating HFO rate, EEG background activity, and MRI findings showed discrimination (AUC = .92, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .69-1.00 for logistic regression; AUC = 1.00, 95% CI = .75-1.00 for random forest), with HFO rate as the strongest contributor to seizure classification.
SIGNIFICANCE: These findings support scalp HFO rate as a potential electrophysiological biomarker of seizure occurrence in neonatal HIE, complementary to EEG background assessment and MRI findings. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether HFOs can predict subsequent seizures.

papers.title: Strengths and weaknesses in epilepsy training across residency programs in Italy: A multicenter survey by the Italian chapter of the Young Epilepsy Section (YES-I).
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of the study was to assess epilepsy-related services across Italian neurology and child neuropsychiatry residency programs, evaluate residents and early-career specialists' perceived strengths/weaknesses in epilepsy training, and identify unmet needs and expectations for improving residency programs and Young Epilepsy Section (YES)-Italy educational initiatives.
METHODS: A nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted between January and April 2026 by a focus group of the YES-Italy Education Task Force. A structured questionnaire was distributed to neurology and child neuropsychiatry residents and specialists within 2 years of completing residency, assessing demographics, epilepsy-related services, self-perceived competencies, training strengths and limitations, and suggestions for improving residency curricula with YES-Italy educational activities. Descriptive statistics were used; group comparisons (neurology vs. child neuropsychiatry; residents vs. early-career specialists) employed the Mann-Whitney U test.
RESULTS: The survey was completed by 150 participants. Epilepsy training was widely available (85.3%) but variable and often brief (<6 months). EEG training was mostly embedded within epilepsy rotation (32.7%), organized as a distinct brief rotation (<3 months; 33.3%), or not available (19.3%). Core epilepsy services were widely present (inpatient wards 82.7%; neurophysiology laboratories 93.3%), while other services were less common (such as epilepsy surgery). Marked variability in Status Epilepticus management emerged across centers. Participants perceived adequate competence for core clinical-diagnostic domains, but lower competence for EEG interpretation and complementary disciplines. Perceived competence was higher in chronic than in acute care. Child neuropsychiatrists reported greater competence in neuropsychology and genetics, neurologists in neuroimaging and acute management. Clinical rotations and multidisciplinary case discussions were major strengths, whereas lectures and direct teaching required improvement. Suggestions for the YES-I group highlighted improving EEG training, structured educational initiatives, access to courses, webinars, and scientific materials.
SIGNIFICANCE: This survey highlights substantial heterogeneity and weaknesses in Italian epilepsy training, particularly regarding EEG interpretation, complementary diagnostics, and acute management, underscoring the need for national standardization, multidisciplinary educational pathways, and strengthened educational initiatives.

papers.title: Promotion and economic considerations of domestic Vagus nerve stimulation within the Chinese three-tier epilepsy center system.
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy affects approximately 10 million people in China, with about 30% developing drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS) is an established neuromodulation therapy for DRE. Domestic VNS devices completed clinical trials in 2014 and entered clinical use in 2016. This study synthesizes clinical outcomes, promotion pathways, and economic considerations of domestic VNS devices within the Chinese three-tier epilepsy center network established by the China Association Against Epilepsy (CAAE).
METHODS: This narrative synthesis integrates data from previously published multicenter prospective real-world studies, CAAE accreditation records, market research, and health economics literature. Clinical outcome data were derived from studies encompassing 124 adult and 87 pediatric patients with DRE across 86 epilepsy centers. A cost comparison between domestic and imported VNS devices was performed based on market data and implantation volumes from 2022-2025.
RESULTS: In adults, responder rates (≥50% seizure reduction) increased progressively from 35.4% at 1 month to 76.6% at 12 months post-implantation, with seizure-free rates reaching 10.9%. In pediatric patients, according to the available follow-up data, ≥50% responder rates (combining seizure freedom, 75% reduction, and 50% reduction) were 43.4% at visit 2, 40.6% at visit 3, 56.6% at visit 4, and 55.8% at visit 5; seizure freedom rates ranged from 1.1 to 9.3% across visits. Significant improvements were observed in sleep quality (PSQI: 5.43 → 4.44), depression (NDDI-E: 6.49 → 4.83), anxiety (GAD-7: 7.15 → 4.95), and quality of life (QOLIE-31: 54.40 → 61.33). Adverse events were mild and transient, primarily voice changes (20.3%) and cough (8.6%). The three-tier network comprises 526 centers (45 Tier-3, 259 Tier-2, 222 Tier-1) with standardized protocols and telemedicine platforms.
CONCLUSION: Domestic VNS demonstrates encouraging efficacy, favorable safety, and improvements in comorbidities in both adult and pediatric DRE populations within the CAAE three-tier network. The network provides a structured framework for standardized application. However, the evidence is limited by the uncontrolled design of the primary studies, short follow-up, and the absence of a formal cost-effectiveness analysis. Prospective comparative clinical and economic validation is warranted.

papers.title: Endothelial glycocalyx remodeling and galectin signaling in aging associated epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Physiological aging can alter the brain endothelial glycocalyx and blood-brain barrier (BBB), while experimental seizures independently engage galectin-3 (Gal-3) and inflammasome-associated inflammatory signaling. This narrative review critically examines whether these observations justify a shared mechanism in aging-associated epilepsy. Primary studies support endothelial mucin-type O-glycosylation as a determinant of BBB integrity and Gal-3 as a modulator of inflammation in selected seizure models. They do not establish that endothelial glycan remodeling changes Gal-3 binding or initiates epileptogenesis. We distinguish extracellular galectin-glycan recognition from intracellular inflammasome signaling and address the anatomical separation between parenchymal microglia and the luminal glycocalyx. Glycan elongation, ligand density, terminal modifications, and steric accessibility could alter binding in different directions; uniform exposure of galectin ligands cannot be assumed. Galectin-1 also has context-dependent protective and detrimental effects. We propose compartment-resolved experiments combining glycan measurements, cell-specific perturbations, BBB assessment, and longitudinal electroencephalography to test the convergence hypothesis.

papers.title: Development of electrochemical aptamer-based sensors for therapeutic monitoring of lamotrigine.
papers.abstract: The anti-epileptic drug lamotrigine has a range of concentrations within which it is effective and unlikely to cause toxicity. However, inter- and intra-individual variation in pharmacokinetics makes it difficult to appropriately dose this drug, necessitating frequent and careful monitoring. Gold-standard quantitative methods such as immunoassays typically require sample preparation, analysis by trained personnel in centralized laboratories and have long turnaround times, rendering them inadequate for timely, convenient, and frequent dose adjustments. To address this issue, we develop an electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensor capable of detecting physiologically relevant concentrations of lamotrigine in unprocessed whole blood. We first discover a new DNA aptamer that binds specifically to lamotrigine with a dissociation constant (K D) of ∼0.8 µM. We then adapted this aptamer in an EAB sensor, demonstrating rapid detection of clinically relevant levels of lamotrigine in whole blood. Importantly, our sensor shows excellent specificity against the major metabolite of lamotrigine, other anti-epileptics, and commonly used pharmaceuticals. With the capability to directly and rapidly quantify lamotrigine in unprocessed blood samples, this EAB sensor represents the simplest, fastest, and most convenient approach to lamotrigine detection to date. With further validation and optimization, the sensor described here could facilitate therapeutic monitoring of lamotrigine at the point-of-care.

papers.title: Diagnostic Odyssey in a Patient with Incontinentia Pigmenti Elucidated by Optical Genome Mapping: A Case Report.
authors: The Brazilian Rare Genomes Project Consortium
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Incontinentia pigmenti is a rare neurocutaneous disorder caused by variants in the IKBKG gene, with X-linked dominant inheritance and a high mortality rate in hemizygous males. This disorder has a characteristic natural history comprising 4 stages (bullous, verrucous, hyperpigmented, and hypopigmented skin lesions); additionally, the phenotypic spectrum is highly variable, and defects in hair, nails, teeth, and other systemic involvements can occur. Molecular confirmation can be performed to detect a common deletion of exons 4-10 in approximately 65% of cases, or sequence variants in less than 10% of cases. However, currently over 20% of cases may still yield a negative molecular result.
CASE PRESENTATION: A female patient was referred due to neurodevelopmental delay, epilepsy, microcephaly, retinal detachment, and cutaneous changes, including diffuse vesiculobullous lesions in the neonatal period evolving in the first year to stable hyperpigmented macules and patches with a blaschkoid distribution. Molecular investigation using different methods, including targeted IKBKG sequencing and short-read whole-genome sequencing, initially ruled out the diagnosis of incontinentia pigmenti and revealed a heterozygous pathogenic variant in the COL7A1 gene, suggesting a diagnosis of transient bullous dermolysis of the newborn. However, persistent molecular investigation using optical genome mapping and long-read whole-genome sequencing confirmed that she had incontinentia pigmenti due to a partial deletion of the IKBKG gene.
CONCLUSION: The case presents the challenges of a diagnostic odyssey and proposes that individuals with incontinentia pigmenti reported as negative for the intragenic deletion should be reanalyzed using long-read technologies.

papers.title: Case Report: Late postpartum eclampsia-associated reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome with anti-DPPX encephalitis.
papers.abstract: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a clinical-radiological syndrome characterized by headaches, seizures, visual disturbances, and focal neurological deficits, accompanied by specific cranial imaging findings. Common triggers of PRES include hypertension/eclampsia, renal disease, autoimmune disorders, and drug abuse. PRES associated with autoimmune encephalitis is a rare phenomenon that presents diagnostic challenges in clinical settings, often leading to missed diagnosis and delayed treatment. We report a case involving a patient with late-onset eclampsia, occurring 26 days after cesarean section, who exhibited dual neurological syndromes of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and anti-DPPX encephalitis. MRI resonance imaging revealed vasogenic cerebral edema and extensive enhancing lesions.

papers.title: The Sv DC Field: Large-Scale and Hierarchical Functions Regulator.
papers.abstract: Large-scale dynamic reorganization of brain functional networks has been extensively revealed by functional magnetic resonance imaging, yet its direct electrophysiological basis remains unclear. In our prior research on epilepsy, we identified a distinctive electrophysiological phenomenon referred to as the slow-varying direct current (Sv DC, 0.01 to 0.5 Hz) field. This field demonstrates both the stability characteristic of a physical direct current and the slow-varying property of bioelectrical signals, enabling it to reflect the dynamic alterations in relative bioelectric field fluctuations. To further characterize its behavior across different functional states, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography from epilepsy patients implanted with depth electrodes during visual, motor, and language tasks. The Sv DC field exhibited large-scale convergence and suppression, accompanied by information transfer to other frequency bands, during these tasks. In visual functional areas, Sv DC field displayed rhythmic oscillations tightly coupled with gamma activity and increased power, whereas in nonvisual areas, Sv DC field power decreased significantly. During seizures, Sv DC field showed characteristic spatiotemporal spreading dynamics, a phenomenon consistently replicated in macaque monkeys, rats, and mice. These electrophysiological patterns suggest that the Sv DC field exhibits both large-scale cortical functional networks and region-specific modulations, potentially offering a novel understanding on dynamic organization of brain functional networks.
